name: Max Carbone
life: “I still remember folding up a bed before its occupant felt ready.” On Monday, near Harbour Bakery, Max buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I wanted the bed free for another patient. I went to see the stairs before asking for a date again.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a pale blue work shirt and a little coil of soft measuring tape. Max has full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side, with a high puff tied with plain cord. Max looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Max has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To give the ward an attainable discharge date.
family: Evelyn Kaur is Max’s half-sibling. Max remembers the birthdays. Evelyn asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The release address*, Evelyn says, “I argued for a homecoming party until he asked for one evening when nobody wanted a speech.”
connections: Neal Heller. The discharge planner hears why a free lift up the stairs isn't the patient's chosen solution.

reactions.situation: A relative offers to carry the patient up the stairs
reactions.response: Max asks the patient whether being carried is an offer they want to take up.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Max keeps the documents out of view and lets the person claiming it identify it before hearing any details.
